Definition: from G104; everduring (forward and backward, or forward only):--eternal, everlasting.
BiblicalUsage: Only twice in the New Testament, and both times of something that never began and never ends. Paul says God's eternal power and Godhead are clearly seen in creation, and Jude says the angels who left their first estate are kept in everlasting chains under darkness. One verse speaks of God's endless nature, the other of an endless judgment.
TheologicalSignificance: The word is too big for anything but God and what God fixes forever. I hold that its force is the contrast: God's eternity is life and glory, while the eternity of judgment is the terrible mirror — what lasts forever depends entirely on whose side of it you stand.
